label: Propofol PK — Schnider (1998)

extraction.tier_rationale: Fixed central volume from a single derivation cohort (n=24, healthy adult volunteers); widely used and externally validated.
Clearance carries the LBM (James 1976) covariate term whose sign drives the high-BMI failure mode.
Schnider effect-site ke0 from the companion PD analysis.
Schnider 1998 Methods: metabolic clearance scales on James (1976) LBM. The negative LBM coefficient composed with James's high-BMI inversion is the documented Schnider-in-obesity failure mode.
extraction.source_locator: Schnider 1998, p. 1503 (Methods, LBM); Table 2 (Cl1 covariate term)

known_failure_modes.behavior: James lean-body-mass term peaks then decreases with rising weight; combined with the negative LBM coefficient in Cl1 this inflates predicted clearance non-physically in obese patients.

predictive_performance.population: external validation, 50 elective surgical adults (head-to-head: Marsh 25%, Schnider 26%, Eleveld 22%)

developmental_model.caveat: Schnider is an adult-only model (derivation age 25-81 y); carrying it into a child by allometry ALONE is a Tier-D extrapolation with NO maturation term — so neonatal/infant clearance is OVER-stated and exposure UNDER-predicted, exactly where the margin is smallest. Prefer a fitted-in-children model, or Eleveld's broad-application model, for pediatric work.

extraction.tier_rationale: Allometric size extrapolation of an adult model; Tier-D by construction (v0.8 §5). Exponents theory-fixed (¾ on clearances, 1 on volumes). No maturation curated for Schnider -> allometry_only, with the over-dose caveat surfaced. Illustrative; awaits human confirmation.

Single robust derivation cohort with extensive external validation; covariate (age/weight/height/LBM) structure broadly recommended. Worst contributing parameter tier is B. Awaits human PDF verification of every covariate equation, especially the James LBM term.

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched open-access reproductions, primary-paper PubMed abstracts, FDA labels, and/or the tci R package source, then numerically compared each curated typical-value parameter against the fetched values (see sources)
sources: schnider-1998-propofol-pk (primary Anesthesiology; paywalled, not directly read)
source_review.notes: All 7 base coefficients (V1 4.27, V2 18.9, V3 238, Cl1 1.89, Cl2 1.29, Cl3 0.836, ke0 0.456) and all covariate slopes (V2 -0.391; Cl1 +0.0456*WGT/-0.0681*LBM/+0.0264*HGT; Cl2 -0.024) confirmed against three fetched sources. NOTE: the tci package mislabels the Cl1 weight term as LBM; the curated dataset CORRECTLY uses WGT, matching the verbatim Schnider equation reproduced in the secondary sources. HUMAN ITEM: confirm against the 1998 Anesthesiology table directly.

notes: Micro-rate constants derived as k10=Cl1/V1, k12=Cl2/V1, k21=Cl2/V2, k13=Cl3/V1, k31=Cl3/V3. LBM via James 1976: male 1.1*W-128*(W/H)^2, female 1.07*W-148*(W/H)^2 (H in cm).
